Subject: Isolation model details for SIG follow-up

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Veridian's audit diary flagged a couple of follow-ups from our SIG submission: we need a short narrative (~1 page) describing how Redwood implements logical and network isolation between Dedicated GPU pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, plus a diagram showing control-plane boundaries and egress policing. The reviewers also asked for any SOC 2 mapping you have that ties isolation controls to Criteria CC6/CC7.

If possible, can you share: 
- A succinct narrative (we can attach to our SIG) that emphasizes the runtime/service-plane separation and where tenant KV caches and model artifacts live.
- A network diagram that annotates control-plane endpoints, customer VPC peering, and outbound egress chokepoints.
- Any index or matrix that maps those controls to SOC 2 criteria (even a CSV is fine).

We have an internal deadline to update the SIG in two business days — would you be able to get drafts to us by Monday EOD PT? If not, let me know the earliest ETA.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Security Architect
Veridian Financial

Hannah / Kim / Alex — draft narrative and attachments attached (stubs below). I focused the narrative on three pillars: control-plane segregation, tenant runtime/serving-plane isolation, and egress chokepoints for data exfil prevention. Key points:

- Control-plane: Customers in Private deployments run a customer-controlled control-plane for private mode (VPC or on-prem). For Redwood Private (VPC-managed option) the management/control APIs are reachable only from customer CIDR blocks and from our management bastions over mTLS; for Dedicated (hosted) the control-plane is multitenant but RBAC and project-scoped management isolate provisioning operations.

- Serving/runtime: Dedicated GPU pools host inference runtimes with strict tenant tags and hardware-enforced isolation at the process/container boundary. KV caches for active request prefixes live in ephemeral in-memory caches on the serving host and are never persisted to cross-tenant shared storage. Model artifacts for hosted Dedicated are stored in per-tenant object namespaces with server-side encryption and customer-key options for Private.

- Egress policing & fallback: Outbound network egress is forced via managed NAT gateways with allowlists; Private option supports VPC routing rules that can force all egress through customer-managed firewalls. We include automatic fallback routing (model variant downgrade) but no automatic outbound calls to external endpoints unless explicitly configured.

Attachments (stubs):
- isolation-narrative-dedicated-private-v1.pdf (1 page)
- network-diagram-v2.png (annotated control-plane + egress)
- soc2_evidence_index.csv (mapping rows: control, description, SOC2 criteria reference)

Link to internal diagram (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/rdw-internal/diagrams/network-diagram-v2.png

Alex — if you want a single slide version or a redline for your SIG, tell me which sections to compress.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
